analysis:
This PR is documentation only: it adds changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md and a paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 508-514). No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

The docs describe a startup Metal kernel shape warmup that runs after model load and self-test, before provider registration and before the local listener opens. It reuses the existing calibration session, idle gate, foreground lease and the same KV and service budgets. It publishes no observations or work totals. The periodic proactive MLX pool sweep defers while a warmup session runs, and on-pressure reclaims still run. It is disabled with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0, or probe-skipped with 'always'.

Security-relevant observations (not findings):
- Availability: warmup adds up to 20 s per model (5.4-7.4 s measured on a cold cache) before registration and listener open. This is bounded and a startup delay only. The 'yields to any request' and foreground-lease claims depend on unsupplied code (IdleCalibrationCoordinator, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibrationRequests), which I could not verify. That contract is a question for a code-level pass. The memory-cap and OS-reserve invariants should not be bypassed, and the docs state that no separate allowance is created.
- Deferring the pool sweep while a session runs could briefly delay cache reclamation. The docs say on-pressure reclaims still run, so no memory-cap regression is evident.
- The warmup uses synthetic prompts, not consumer data, so there is no A-001 exposure and no interaction with the prefix cache (T-041). I cannot confirm from the docs that warmup cells do not donate to the SSD prefix cache. A code-level review should confirm that synthetic warmup prompts are not persisted or donated to the SSD tier.
- T-028 (residual GPU memory) is unaffected in kind.

No threat-model update is required from the documentation alone. The code change implementing this was not supplied.
